recipes.name: Masala Fish Curry (Salmon/Mackerel)
recipes.health_benefit: This recipe is rich in Omega-3 fatty acids, which may help support healthy cholesterol levels and cardiovascular health. Fatty fish like salmon and mackerel are also excellent natural sources of Vitamin D, crucial for bone health and immune function.
instructions: Cut fish into desired pieces, wash and pat dry. Marinate with a pinch of turmeric and salt for 10 minutes.
Heat mustard oil in a pan. Add chopped onions and sauté until golden brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste and green chili, sauté for 1 minute until aromatic.
Stir in pureed tomatoes and cook until the oil separates, about 5-7 minutes.
Add turmeric, red chili, coriander, and cumin powders. Sauté for 2-3 minutes, adding a splash of water if needed to prevent burning.
Add 1 cup of water (or half water, half light coconut milk for a richer gravy) and salt. Bring to a simmer.
Gently add the marinated fish pieces to the gravy. Cover and cook for 5-7 minutes, or until fish is cooked through.
Sprinkle with garam masala and fresh coriander leaves. Serve hot with brown rice.

recipes.name: Dal Palak (Lentil and Spinach Curry)
recipes.health_benefit: This recipe is an excellent source of dietary fiber and plant-based protein, which are beneficial for managing cholesterol levels and promoting digestive health. Spinach adds essential vitamins and minerals, supporting overall well-being.

ingredients.item: Toor Dal (split pigeon peas) or Masoor Dal (red lentils)

instructions: Wash and soak dal for 20-30 minutes. Cook dal with 2 cups of water, turmeric, and a pinch of salt in a pressure cooker until soft (2-3 whistles). Mash lightly.
Heat oil/ghee in a separate pan. Add cumin seeds and asafoetida. Once they splutter, add chopped onion and sauté until translucent.
Add ginger-garlic paste and green chili, sauté for 1 minute.
Add chopped tomato, red chili powder, and coriander powder. Cook until tomatoes soften and oil separates.
Add the chopped spinach and cook until it wilts completely.
Pour the cooked dal into the spinach mixture. Add water if needed to adjust consistency. Bring to a simmer.
Check for salt. Garnish with fresh coriander leaves. Serve hot with brown rice or whole wheat roti.

recipes.name: Ragi Porridge with Nuts and Berries
recipes.health_benefit: Ragi (finger millet) is a whole grain rich in dietary fiber, which can help in managing cholesterol. This porridge, made with fortified plant milk and nuts, provides a good source of Vitamin D, healthy fats, and sustained energy for the day.
instructions: In a saucepan, mix ragi flour with 0.5 cup water to form a smooth paste, ensuring no lumps.
Add the fortified milk to the ragi paste. Place on medium heat and stir continuously to prevent lumps.
Cook for 5-7 minutes until the porridge thickens and the raw smell of ragi disappears.
Stir in jaggery powder or dates syrup for sweetness. Cook for another minute.
Pour the porridge into a bowl. Garnish with chopped almonds, walnuts, mixed berries, and chia seeds.
Serve warm.

recipes.name: Chicken and Vegetable Stir-fry
recipes.health_benefit: This stir-fry provides lean protein for muscle health and satiety, combined with a variety of vegetables for essential vitamins, minerals, and dietary fiber. It's cooked with minimal oil to support healthy cholesterol management.
instructions: Heat oil in a large wok or pan over high heat.
Add chicken strips and stir-fry until cooked through and lightly browned (about 5-7 minutes). Remove chicken and set aside.
In the same pan, add onions and stir-fry for 1 minute. Add ginger-garlic paste and stir-fry for another minute.
Add broccoli, bell peppers, and carrots. Stir-fry for 3-5 minutes until vegetables are crisp-tender.
Return the cooked chicken to the pan. Add low-sodium soy sauce, black pepper, and salt (if needed).
Toss everything together until well combined and heated through.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves. Serve hot, optionally with a small portion of brown rice.

recipes.name: Sprouted Moong Chaat
recipes.health_benefit: This chaat is a fiber and protein powerhouse, contributing to satiety and aiding in cholesterol management. Sprouting enhances nutrient availability, making it a highly nutritious and refreshing snack option.
instructions: Gently boil or steam the sprouted moong beans for 5-7 minutes until slightly tender but still crunchy. Drain well and let cool.
In a mixing bowl, combine the cooled sprouted moong with chopped onion, tomato, cucumber, green chili (if using), and fresh coriander.
Add lemon juice, chaat masala, black salt, and roasted cumin powder.
Toss everything together gently until all ingredients are well combined and coated with the spices.
Taste and adjust seasonings as needed. Serve immediately.

recipes.name: Vegetable Pulao with Brown Rice
recipes.health_benefit: Utilizing brown rice, this pulao offers complex carbohydrates and significantly more fiber than white rice, which is beneficial for gut health and LDL cholesterol management. The abundance of vegetables further boosts its nutrient profile.

ingredients.item: Whole spices (bay leaf, cinnamon stick, cloves, green cardamom)

ingredients.quantity: 2 cups (or as per brown rice package instructions)

instructions: Wash brown rice thoroughly and soak for at least 30 minutes, then drain.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pan or pressure cooker. Add whole spices and sauté for a few seconds until fragrant.
Add sliced onions and sauté until translucent. Add ginger-garlic paste and green chilies, cook for 1 minute.
Add the chopped mixed vegetables, turmeric powder, cumin powder, and salt. Sauté for 3-5 minutes.
Add the soaked and drained brown rice to the pan. Gently mix for 1 minute.
Pour in 2 cups of water (or as specified for brown rice) and bring to a boil. Add garam masala.
If using a pan: Cover tightly, reduce heat to low, and cook for 25-30 minutes until water is absorbed and rice is tender. If using a pressure cooker: Cook for 2-3 whistles on medium heat.
Once cooked, let it rest for 5 minutes before fluffing with a fork. Garnish with fresh coriander leaves.
Serve hot with raita or dal.
